seoTitle: Channel Letter Signs: Types, Lighting & Mounting Guide
seoDescription: Compare front-lit, halo-lit, reverse, and dual-lit channel letter signs. Sizing, raceway vs flush mounting, LED power draw, and storefront permits explained.
summary: Channel letter signs are custom 3D exterior signs fabricated from sheet metal and acrylic, powered by low-voltage LEDs. The four main styles are front-lit for daylight contrast and nighttime punch, halo-lit (reverse) for an upscale architectural back-glow, dual-lit for combined illumination, and open-face. Your choice hinges on facade type, viewing distance, and raceway vs. flush mounting.
secondaryKeywords: front lit vs halo lit channel letters
channel letters raceway mount vs flush mount
keyTakeaways: Front-lit channel letters maximize long-distance readability using translucent acrylic faces and internal LEDs, making them the standard choice for busy retail corridors.
Halo-lit (reverse) channel letters project light backward onto the mounting surface via stainless steel standoffs, creating an upscale architectural aura ideal for boutiques and restaurants.
Dual-lit channel letters combine illuminated acrylic faces with halo backlighting, providing maximum visual contrast and high-end brand impact at night.
Raceway mounting groups all letters and power supplies into a single pre-wired metal housing, minimizing exterior building penetrations and satisfying strict commercial landlord criteria.
Flush (direct) mounting anchors each letter individually through the facade for a seamless look, but requires rear wall access to route Class 2 low-voltage wiring.
